$comment: Ceilings on the STATIC IMPORT GRAPH, checked by scripts/perf/check-budget.mjs
(`npm run perf:budget`) and held on every push by the last two cases of
scripts/perf/__tests__/check-budget.test.mjs, which CI already runs as test:perf.
What it measures is cost per REQUEST rather than bundle size: Next compiles a
route s entire module graph on first hit with no tree-shaking, so the number of
first-party modules on a path tracks what an operator waits for almost linearly.
THESE NUMBERS WERE MEASURED, not chosen — `--record` walked this tree and wrote
each ceiling as the measurement plus slackPercent (15). Ordinary growth does not
trip them; a doubling does. `--tighten` lowers them to what the tree costs today
and can never raise one.
The group ceiling is the p95 route, not the worst: one fat route must not buy
headroom for all 200. A route above the p95 gets a named override with its own
measured ceiling, so it is visible in the diff instead of hidden under a
generous number. `overrides` being empty means no route was an outlier.
THE BARREL RULE HAS NO SLACK, on purpose. `maxValueImporters` is the exact count
at the time of recording: importing app/_lib/db.ts FOR VALUE drags all 17 store
modules into the importer and everything downstream of it, so the 28th importer
is meant to stop and import the slice instead (`import type` is erased before
bundling and is not counted). Raising this number is a decision, not a fix.
Raising any ceiling is an edit to this file with a why a reviewer can disagree
with. `npm run perf:budget -- --explain <path>` shows what is on a path.
